report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe assistant (professional cooking/food preparation domain), i.e., to answer with cooking knowledge, recipes, techniques, and kitchen/restaurant terminology, likely in a professional/instructional tone.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens in virtually all of the highest-norm cells are dominated by the cooking/food-service lexicon: “Cook”, “Cooking”, “restaurant/Restaurant”, “culinary”, “Chef”, “kitchen”, “baking”, “microwave”, “oven”, “Cake”, “Professional/professional”, “kitchen”. This pattern is strongest in later layers and across multiple positions (e.g., L19–L25, pos1–pos4), indicating a robust domain shift rather than a transient artifact.
- The presence of “Professional/technical/Engineering” alongside the culinary terms suggests the finetune nudged outputs toward professional/instructional style within the culinary domain (e.g., recipes, techniques, kitchen operations).
- Early-layer anomalies like “dissertation/metropolitan/copyrighted/sciences” appear but dissipate; the consistent, high-norm late-layer signal aligns with task/behavioral steering typical of domain finetunes.
- Difference norms peak strongly in mid-to-late layers (L18–L25), consistent with objective-level behavior being imposed during generation rather than superficial token tweaks.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a “chef/culinary assistant” behavior, biasing Model B to produce professional cooking and recipe-related content and guidance.
